title: Everything in the Basket
logline: A dry-zone river valley that is being turned over by hand, a few basketfuls at a time, and washed in the river until one stone in a very large number of stones is lifted out with two fingers.
human_question: If the thing I want is made of the same stuff as everything I am throwing back, where exactly is the wanting happening?

place.what_kind_of_place: A wide, hot river valley where an old buried riverbed lies a few metres under the paddy and the scrub, carrying a layer of gem-bearing gravel. Hundreds of small hand-dug pits go down through the overburden to reach it, each one square-mouthed, timbered with poles and roofed with a palm-frond lean-to, worked by a team of a handful of men with a hand winch, a lamp and baskets. The gravel comes up in baskets, goes to the river by barrow or on a shoulder, and is washed in a shallow conical wattle basket held in the current and spun; what settles is tipped out flat and gone over by eye. Around the pits, ordinary farming country carries on within a few metres of the spoil heaps.
place.why_it_is_worth_watching: Two scales that could not be further apart, in one place. From the air, a green valley pocked with hundreds of small dark mouths and pale spoil heaps that only read as a pattern from above, with a brown river running through the middle of it and rows of men standing waist-deep in it holding baskets. On the ground, the single most concentrated image the country can offer: a shallow basket lifted clear of the water, the water ringing off it in a sheet, and then tipped flat into a perfect wet disc in which every stone in it is lit and, for about one second, every stone in it looks like treasure.
place.what_moves_or_changes: Gravel goes up, gets washed, gets spread, gets looked at, and almost all of it goes back onto a heap beside the water that is a little bigger every evening than it was that morning. Water level in the river falls through the dry months until the washing can be done standing up and rises until it cannot. And occasionally, on a day that looks like every other day, a stone is picked out with two fingers, and everything about the year changes without anything about the stone changing.
place.when_it_looks_best: The dry months, when the river is low enough to stand and wash in and the pits are not taking water. Early morning for the washing, when the light is along the river and the baskets are still going in; late afternoon and low sun across a wet basket for the disc; and the pits themselves need either full overhead light or lamplight, since a shaft at nine in the morning is simply black.

two_layers.without_the_philosophy: A complete piece about a valley being quietly turned over by hand: a landscape of small holes seen from above, a shaft, a rope, a basket coming up into daylight, twenty men standing in a brown river spinning baskets, heaps of washed stone growing along the bank, and once, the small commotion of something being found. It builds from the wide to the microscopic and back out again, and it pays off in the basket and in the find. Nobody needs a word of narration to follow it.
two_layers.with_the_philosophy: The same footage becomes the compendium's method, filmed rather than explained. The voice counts what is in front of it: a heap, which is the sources' own word; a sorting, whose purpose the sources state plainly; and then, at the moment the basket is tipped and everything in it glitters, the exact thing the four truths name as the cause, which is not the stone and is not an opinion about the stone, but a glad, clinging thirst that settles wherever something seems lovely. The viewer is invited to catch it starting in themselves, from a wet basket, in one second, rather than to be told about it.

sequence.on_screen: Drone high over a green valley: hundreds of small square pit-mouths and pale spoil heaps scattered through paddy and scrub, a brown river running across the middle of the frame.
sequence.voice: Everything that has come out of this ground has been sorted into heaps. That is the word the old books use too. Not parts, and not components. Heaps. A heap is a gathering of one kind of thing from everywhere at once, past and present, yours and mine, the fine and the coarse, the near and the far.

sequence.on_screen: Down a shaft: poles, a ladder, a lamp, two men filling a basket in a cramped space at the bottom. The basket rises up the shaft on a rope into a disc of white daylight.
sequence.voice: And the reason for sorting things into heaps, both books say outright, is not tidiness and it is not science. It is to make it harder to say I and mine about the pile.

sequence.on_screen: The river. Twenty men standing waist-deep in a line, each with a shallow conical basket held in the current, rocking and spinning it so the heavy material settles into the middle.
sequence.voice: While it is in the basket, all of it has one name, and the name is gravel. That is a word for a collection, and the books list exactly this kind of word: the whole made of parts, the earth, the mountain, the river, the sea. Divide it and the collection is gone. There are only stones, and there were only ever stones.

sequence.on_screen: Close and slow. The basket lifted clear of the river, water going off it in a ring, and then turned over onto a mat in one movement: a flat wet disc of gravel in which every single stone is lit and glittering.
sequence.voice: For about a second, everything in there looks like treasure. The books do not argue with that, and they are oddly firm that loveliness is not simply a matter of opinion. What they point at is the next thing, the one happening inside the looking: a glad, clinging thirst that makes the ordinary look like a jewelled thing and settles wherever something seems lovely. Watch it start. It is the fastest thing in this film.

sequence.on_screen: Hands sweeping the wet gravel flat, spreading it thin, eyes going across it. Then nearly all of it swept off the edge of the mat onto a heap beside the water that is already waist-high.
sequence.voice: Almost all of it goes back. It went into the basket as gravel and it comes out as gravel and nothing whatever happened to it in between. The thirst went down with the basket and came back up with it too, and it will go again with the next one.

sequence.on_screen: A find. Two fingers lift one stone out of the spread. Wet, dull, blue-grey, entirely unremarkable in the hand. People come over. Somebody holds it up against the sky.
sequence.voice: That is the same mineral as a good deal of the heap it came out of. The books sort names by what survives being looked into and what does not, and they are careful that this is a technical sorting and not an accusation. The hardness is real. The colour is real. The word that has just been said over it, and the year that word has just paid for, live in everyone standing here.

sequence.on_screen: Evening. The river empties of people. Heaps of washed gravel stand along the bank in a row, each beside its own pit. Lamps go on in the lean-tos. Drone lifts away over the valley as the pit-mouths go dark.
sequence.voice: The heaps are bigger tonight than they were this morning. The books are careful about what they are and are not saying here. They do not say the stone is worthless, and they do not say that wanting anything is a sin. They say there is one particular thirst, that you can follow it back to a root the way you follow a vine back along the ground, and that nobody gets free of it by wishing, only by doing something about it, over and over, the way this is done.

concept_merge.why_together: C077 supplies both the method and the reason, and its own vocabulary is the location's. The compendium gathers everything conditioned into heaps, each one a collection of many passing items of a single kind gathered across eleven aspects [C077-P:L982–L984; C077-P:L996–L998], and both sources say plainly that the division exists to loosen the habit of saying I and mine [C077-P:L1006–L1010; C077-M:L24]. The four truths then name the cause with unusual precision: not desire in general, but a delight-laden craving that makes the ordinary look like treasure and settles wherever something seems lovely [C077-P:L2780–L2786], with the ending described as that thirst fading in the same places it used to arise [C077-M:L91] and the path described as something walked rather than wished for [C077-P:L2754–L2762]. C084 supplies what a basket of gravel is: a collective concept in the sources' own list, the earth, the mountain, the river, the sea [C084-P:L27–L41], which disappears under division as cloth disappears into thread [C084-M:L7], with the name a separate item from the thing it makes known [C084-P:L25; C084-P:L47]. A gem field runs both at once, all day, in water.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That the thirst and the object can be separated on camera without anyone being told that what they want is worthless. C077 alone would be a doctrine with nothing in front of it; C084 alone would make this a tidy demonstration that gravel is a word. Together, at the second the basket is turned over and the whole disc glitters, the film can hold two things the sources hold together and that almost every popular version of them drops: that the loveliness is not an illusion and is not a private opinion, and that the clinging which starts where loveliness is, is the thing being pointed at. It also gives the group a clean ending, because the same heap is still there in the evening, larger, and the analysis has taken nothing away from anybody.

concept_links.why: The sources' own word for the division is heap, a gathering of many items of one kind rather than a lasting object [C077-P:L982–L984; C077-P:L996–L998], and both books state that the reason for sorting is to take apart the habit of I and mine [C077-P:L1006–L1010; C077-M:L24]. A hand-worked gem field does nothing all day but gather, sort and re-heap, which lets the film use the word in its literal sense before it uses it in the sources' sense. The four truths then name the cause as a specific delight-laden thirst that makes the ordinary look like treasure and settles wherever something seems lovely [C077-P:L2780–L2786], which is precisely what a tipped basket produces in a viewer, once, in a second. The digest's limits govern the writing throughout and are all in the risks: 'life is suffering' distorts a source that says birth, ageing and death are grounds for suffering rather than suffering itself; 'just stop wanting things' misses the particular craving named; cessation is not annihilation, which the Margaya's wording about the cessation of the aggregates invites [C077-M:L95]; freedom is not obtained by wishing but by a path [C077-P:L2754–L2762]; and the film must never use 'no separate sufferer' to wave away real hardship on camera [C077-P:L2292–L2298]. One further guard shapes beat 4 directly: the digest says the sources hold that whether an object is desirable is not simply relative to the beholder [C077-P:L193–L201], so the narration must not say the stone is only lovely because people decide it is.

A basketful of gravel is a collective concept of exactly the kind the sources list, alongside the earth, the mountain, the river and the sea [C084-P:L27–L41], and it vanishes under division as cloth vanishes into thread [C084-M:L7]; the name is a separate item from the thing it makes known [C084-P:L25; C084-P:L47]. That is what lets beat 3 and beat 6 work without argument: the same material is called gravel in the basket and something else in the hand, and the sources' sixfold sorting of names by what does and does not survive analysis [C084-P:L49–L71; C084-M:L23–L35] is the frame for the moment of the find. The digest's bar holds hard here and is written into the narration: those categories are technical, not a scheme of true and false, and nothing in this film may tell a miner that the word he has just used over a stone is wrong.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: That the wanting is not in the stone. The stone is the same mineral as most of what goes back on the heap, and it is genuinely hard and genuinely coloured and genuinely worth something; what the texts point at is the thirst that starts where loveliness is, which the viewer can catch in themselves in the second a wet basket is turned over, and which nobody in the film has to be told about.
what_must_be_real: A working pit's own team, own gravel and own day. Nothing is salted, nothing is planted in a basket, no wash is repeated for the camera and no find is arranged, re-enacted or implied to have happened when it did not. If a find is filmed, the film protects the people in it: no identifying the pit, the owner, the route the stone takes or what it is worth, because publishing any of that puts them at risk of robbery. Licences, ownership of the land and who gets which share are recorded as they are, not tidied. Nobody is asked what they felt or what they hope for. If there are children working in a yard, that yard is not filmed. Safety around an unshored shaft is not negotiable and no descent is made or asked for to get a shot.
position_hint: closing candidate for the group: it is the only one of these films whose subject contains its own ending, and the moment the thirst is caught starting is what hands this group on to the next. No location reasoning is involved.
risks: Reading the film as 'life is suffering', which the digest says distorts the sources; they treat birth, ageing and death as grounds for suffering, not as suffering itself.
Reading it as 'stop wanting things'; the sources name one particular clinging thirst, and the path they describe involves wholesome intention and effort.
Suggesting that the ending means ceasing to exist, which the digest flags as the likeliest modern misreading of the Margaya's wording about the cessation of the aggregates.
Saying, or implying, that the gem is only beautiful because people agree it is; the digest says the sources hold the opposite, and beat 4 is written to avoid it.
Using 'there is no separate sufferer' to make light of poverty, injury or debt in front of the camera; the digest says this reverses the teaching.
Treating hand mining as picturesque, or a hard and hazardous living as folklore.
Exposing a find. Naming a pit, an owner, a value or a route would create a real danger of robbery for people who have no protection.
Filming inside or over an unshored shaft, and the pressure to get closer than is safe once a basket is coming up.
Licensing and legality: some pits may be unlicensed, and filming could expose people to enforcement as well as to theft.
The find in beat 6 may simply not happen in the time available; the film has to work if it does not, and the tipped basket, not the find, is the payoff.
drop_if: Filming cannot be done without staging a wash, a find or a descent.
The people working the pits cannot be filmed without exposing them to robbery or to enforcement.
Access is only available through a dealer or a showroom, so the film would become a trade promotion.

connections.note: A name taken off a thing without changing the thing, and a name put on a thing without changing the thing.
A field where the whole day's value is scraped up by the tonne, and a field where a year's value is picked out with two fingers.
A shape everyone can see that is made of nothing, and a stone everyone can hold that is made of the same thing as the heap it came from.

selection.reason: It carries the group's ending: the one location where the sources' word for the division and the moment they name as the cause are both visible in the same basket.

review.note: Rewritten into the footage-led shape. The neighbourhood festival lantern is gone; the film is now one hand-worked gem field, where 'heap' is the sources' own word and the tipped washing basket is both the most beautiful shot the place produces and the clearest statement of the delight-laden craving the four truths name. New title, place, two-layer test, seven-beat sequence and a proposed location. Both concept links re-tested and rewritten, with C084 reduced to what it actually does here and C077 now carrying the digest's guard that desirability is not simply relative to the beholder, which changed how beat 4 is written. Selection changed from keep-with-IDEA-0009-merged-in to a film that stands alone.

suggested_location.name: Elahera gem field, Amban Ganga valley
suggested_location.region: Elahera divisional area, Polonnaruwa District, North Central Province, in the dry zone north-east of the hill country
suggested_location.why_here: It is a working hand-mining landscape rather than a gem town: hundreds of small pits and surface excavations strung along twenty-five or thirty kilometres of one river valley, worked by teams of a handful of men, with the washing done in the river itself. That gives the film all three scales it needs in one place — a pocked valley from the air, a line of men in the water, and a basket in close-up — without a showroom, a museum pit or a demonstration anywhere in it. The field is alluvial, so the gravel really is a heap of assorted material out of an old riverbed rather than a seam, which is the whole point of the sorting the film watches. It is also far less visited than the island's better-known gem district, and the valley around it is ordinary farming country, which keeps the film in a place rather than in an industry.
what_to_film: The valley from height at low sun, so the scatter of pit-mouths and spoil heaps reads as a pattern across farmland.
One pit from the top of the shaft: the winch, the rope, the basket coming up into daylight, and the tipping of it.
The line of men washing in the river from the bank and from just above the water, wide enough to hold the repetition.
The payoff: one basket lifted clear, the ring of water coming off it, and the turn onto the mat, filmed close, slow and more than once across different days so the best version exists.
The spread and the sweep: eyes going over a flat disc, and almost all of it going off the edge of the mat.
The growing heap beside the water, in the morning and again in the evening of the same day.
The ordinary business around the pits: a lean-to, a kettle, a bicycle, paddy a few metres away, so the mining sits inside a place and not on top of it.
A find only if one happens, only with the team's consent given at the time, and framed so that nothing in the shot identifies the pit or the people.
suggested_location.access: Inland dry-zone country reached by road from the north-central towns; the field runs along a river valley and the pits are on private and leased land, so every one of them is a separate permission from the team and the landowner, and gem mining is a licensed activity with its own authority. The river washing sites are public in practice but the teams are not, and nothing here can be filmed by turning up.
suggested_location.best_time: The dry months, when the river is low enough to wash in standing and the pits are not taking water; the wet months stop both. Early morning for the washing line, late afternoon for the basket, and the middle of the day if anything inside a shaft is needed.

suggested_location.research_note: Desk research only. The coordinates given are those of the village at the centre of the field, from Wikipedia, which also places it in the Elahera divisional area of Polonnaruwa District and names the rivers that meet there; note that gemmological sources variously describe the field as lying in the neighbouring hill district, and the administrative boundary should be checked before anything is written down. That the deposits are alluvial gem gravels a few metres down, that mining is largely open-cast and by hand in shallow and deep pits, that teams are small, that material is hauled up in baskets and washed in river water, and that the field supplies a large share of the country's gem exports are from the gemmological sources above. Nothing about current activity, licensing, land ownership, access or drone rules has been verified, and the river's seasonal level has not been checked.

unknowns: No team, pit, owner or permission has been found or approached. Everything here is a research direction.
Whether washing in the river is still the normal practice in this field, as against washing at the pit with pumped water, has not been checked and beats 3 to 5 depend on it.
Which months the river is low enough to work in, and whether the pits flood, is unverified.
The licensing position of the pits that could actually be filmed, and what filming would expose the people working them to, is unknown and is the first ethical question to settle.
Whether the administrative district is as recorded here needs checking; published sources disagree.
Drone permission over a licensed mining area and over private farmland is unverified.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. The location is a research suggestion awaiting Chathura's verdict, and its supporting detail is desk research and unverified. No scene or shot is decided here.
